svg.title: Koszul towers, torsion and full derived completion
svg.desc: Strict relative power thickenings have a conservative first reduction. After that reduction, transition maps kill the additional exterior generators, proving the entire unbounded module counit. Koszul torsion, quasicoherent sheaves on the formal completion and derived complete modules are equivalent. Formal affine exterior tensors are computed by their actual compact Koszul generators. The examples retain derived module actions and a noncompact unit.
svg.text: The whole module tower is controlled by its first reduction
Connective complex DG B; finite degree-zero equations f; modules unbounded in both directions.
1. A relative semifree model makes the powers strict — KTC.1–KTC.3
P = C[t₁,…,tᵣ] → Q ≃ B; B(N) = Q/(t₁ᴺ,…,tᵣᴺ).
Q is graded-free over P, with an exhaustive semifree module filtration.
The t-adic finite filtration of B(N) has graded pieces finite sums of B(1).
Length ≤ r(N−1)+1: reduction from B(N)-modules to B(1)-modules is conservative.
No cohomological bound on a module is used.
2. Extra exterior generators disappear in the inverse system — KTC.4–KTC.10
D(N,1) = B(N) ⊗ᴸ over B with B(1) = B(1)[η₁,…,ηᵣ], |ηᵢ| = −1.
For N′ > N: ηᵢ at N′ maps to tᵢ^(N′−N) ηᵢ = 0 over B(1).
For a coherent system M(N): M(N) ⊗ᴸ B(1) ≃ M(1) ⊗ Λ(η₁,…,ηᵣ).
identity
positive exterior summands
zero
Perfect B(1) commutes with the inverse limit; the actual counit reduces to M(1).
Conservativity at every stage proves F G ≃ identity on the whole category of systems.
3. Three actual categories and their inverse functors — KTC.11–KTC.21
C(f) = ⊗ᵢ fib(B → B[fᵢ⁻¹]); Γ(M) = C(f) ⊗ᴸ M; Λ(M) = RHom(C(f),M).
torsion modules
QCoh(formal completion)
complete modules
F ≃
G ≃
Inverse to F: Γ G. Inverse to G: restriction F on the complete category.
Torsion unit = C(f); complete unit = Λ(B); complete tensor = Λ(M ⊗ᴸ N).
K(f) is a compact generator. The unit need not be compact.
Empty equation list gives Mod B; a unit equation gives the zero category.
4. The formal affine exterior tensor is the canonical one — KTC.22–KTC.24
K(f) ⊗ K(g) = K(f,g): finite perfect Hom complexes tensor exactly over C.
The free-module bars identify the supported categories and their product category.
QCoh(Ŷ(f)) ⊗ QCoh(Ŷ(g)) ≃ QCoh(Ŷ(f) × Ŷ(g)).
The filtered restricted union and H-quotient still require their global comparisons.
5. Tests that distinguish the full theorem from truncation — KTC.25–KTC.37
Zero equation: every stage has an odd class, but its transition is zero.
M = C[z,z⁻¹], |z| = −2, has classes in every even integer degree; G F(M) = M.
Formal disc: torsion unit has H¹ = t⁻¹ C[t⁻¹]; complete unit is C[[t]].
No tᴺ kills all principal parts: the actual quasicoherent unit is not compact.
F(C)(N) has an exterior class with its full derived module action.
A constant ordinary C is not a system: C ⊗ᴸ over C[t]/t² with C has H⁻ⁿ = C, n ≥ 0.
Two variables retain degree-two principal parts and the completed two-variable series.
Exact proof locators: §§3.158–3.166, KTC.1–KTC.37; Solutions3.CW–3.CZ.
Formal-completion framework: AGKRRV, arXiv:2010.01906v2.
